title: Ephemeral refactor safety & follow-ups (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for approaching small–to–medium refactors that touch the hot path (request routing, batching, kv-cache interop) or developer ergonomics near serving runtime. Goal: fast iteration but reduce post-merge surprises and long tail customer impact.

High-level approach (short):
- Assume any change that can alter latency distribution or cache keys needs safety gates.
- Prefer layered rollouts (canary -> small % -> wider) if the change affects runtime code paths.
- Keep PRs small and annotated with the exact safety checks required.

Quick pre-review checklist (things I scan first):
- Scope: does diff touch runtime/serving or only UX/docs? If runtime, require perf numbers.
- Tests: unit + integration + a simple local perf/latency script present? If not, ask for a micro-benchmark.
- Observable changes: new metrics? Will old metrics still make sense? Are there metric name changes?
- Cache keys: any change to request normalization, hashing, prefixing, or metadata that could change cache hits?
- Backwards compatibility: wire format, API fields, model routing decisions.
- Safety nets: feature flag, canary config, or automatic fallback on errors/timeouts.

Concrete heuristics I use in comments on PRs:
- "If you change this normalization, add a toggle + reason. We can’t afford a silent cache drop for prod traffic"
- "Instrument with a histogram for latencies and ensure p50/p95/p99 are tracked by route/model"
- "Add an integration test that mirrors the expected KV-load for this path (e.g., populate kv with 1k keys)."

Micro-bench commands I ask contributors to run (local):
- run perf harness for the path: ./infra/tools/perf_client --route rerank-v1 --batch-size 8 --seq-len 512
- simple latency histogram: go run ./tools/latency_probe/main.go --route=chat --duration=1m --concurrency=16
- smoke load against canary: k6 run smoke-canary.js --vus 20 --duration 2m (attach baseline run)

Minimal PR description template I paste in reviews:
- What changed (1-2 lines)
- Why (user/infra reason)
- Risk profile (low/medium/high) and why
- Required test/perf artifacts (links to perf run, test run)
- Rollout plan (feature flag/canary %/fallback)

Safety rollout checklist (if change risk != low):
- Add feature-flag gate in code and config.
- Create canary deployment (1–2 nodes) in staging & prod-canary.
- Monitor these metrics for 30m after deploy: qps, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, cache hit rate, memory/GPU utilization.
- If any metric regresses >10% at p95 or error rate increases, rollback automatically after 5 failures.
- Post-canary: expand to 20% for 1 hour, then evaluate.

Instrumentation / Metrics I insist on (minimum):
- route.request.latency.{p50,p95,p99}
- route.request.errors.count
- cache.{hit,miss}.rate by route+model
- runtime.queue.length and runtime.batching.size
- memory/allocs per request (if change touches KV or buffer allocation)

Test ideas to prevent silent regressions:
- deterministic cache-compat test: run a set of synthetic requests, assert cache hit pattern unchanged after the change.
- golden-output smoke test for a small prompt set to detect quality drift when request normalization changes.
- quick fuzz of headers/metadata to ensure routing logic is tolerant.

Refactor mapping (for follow-ups):
- Extract: listener adapter plumbing (will allow easier canary toggles) -> owner: Nora -> ticket TICKET-8050
- Isolate: KV-key normalization logic into a single util with migration tests -> owner: Jaden -> TICKET-8062
- Observe: add per-route batching histograms and expose via Console -> owner: SRE/OBS -> TICKET-8087

Post-merge follow-ups I typically add to the PR before merging:
- Add canary config and rollout note to the PR body (short snippet with percentages).
- File a follow-up ticket to add a short-lived regression alert for 24–72 hours (who: oncall).
- Add a small smoke test in the e2e suite that runs once in CI-weekly (to catch slow degradations).

Rollback playbook (to link in PR):
- If canary fails: revert the change via rollback tag to the previous image, keep canary traffic on rollback image, notify #serving-runtime.
- If gradual rollout fails: flip feature flag off and trigger scale-in of stable pool.
- If silent user-facing degradation observed (not flagged): coordinate with SRE to throttle traffic and snapshot traces for triage.

Notes to self (open questions / recent learnings):
- Should we standardize on a single 'cache_v1' namespace vs embedding route+model in key? Embedding is more selective but harder to migrate.
- For small refactors that touch the hot path, require at least one perf run at batch-size 1 and batch-size typical (8–32) to ensure no unintended linearization.
- We still lack a good local reproduction harness for KV cache warm/cold cycles. Prioritize a small tool that simulates warm cache + eviction pattern.

Example comment I leave on risky PRs (short):
"Thanks — this looks functionally correct. Before merging: can you attach a perf run (local or k6) comparing master vs this branch for seq-len 128/512 and batch sizes 1 & 16, and add a short canary plan to the PR? Also add a quick integration test that asserts cache hit rate isn't reduced by >5% on the synthetic set."

TODO (next actions from this note):
- Build a tiny cache-sim harness (Jaden) - estimate 2d.
- Draft a standard 'refactor-risk' PR checklist template in repo CONTRIBUTING.md (pair with Nora) - estimate 1d.
- Create an internal gist with perf-run commands + script wrappers for non-systems folks - estimate 0.5d.

Random snippets I paste in PRs (copy & paste friendly):
- Perf run script example: ./infra/tools/perf_client --route=chat --seq-len=512 --batch-size=8 --duration=60s > perf_before.txt
- Canary config example block:
  - canary: enabled
  - canary_percent: 5
  - canary_duration_minutes: 30

End notes:
This is intentionally terse. Keep PRs small, demand perf evidence for hot-path changes, and make rollouts reversible. I’ll update this after the next week of PRs if patterns need to change.

-- Jaden
